title: Swahili for English speakers
description: Swahili is East Africa’s shared language, spoken by tens of millions from Mombasa and Zanzibar to Kampala, Kigali and Goma.
notes: Drafted by Claude (AI) in standard Swahili (Kiswahili sanifu) and needs a native-speaker review: see the checklist in journal/2026-10-22-swahili-course.md. Where Kenyan and Tanzanian usage differ (matatu or daladala, for example), both are accepted and the notes say so. Sections are added one at a time toward 40 units (#146).

why.title: One language for **all of East Africa.**
why.text: Swahili is an official language of Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and the East African Community, and the everyday lingua franca from the Indian Ocean coast to the Congo. Learn it to travel, trade, make friends and follow the music, from taarab to bongo flava.

cards.title: For travellers
cards.text: Get around from Mombasa to Mwanza, by matatu, daladala or ferry.

cards.title: For work
cards.text: Talk with colleagues and customers across the whole region.

cards.title: For the curious
cards.text: Meet noun classes, proverbs and a thousand years of coastal poetry.

landing.farewell: Asante sana — thank you very much.
landing.audience: Complete beginners, travellers and volunteers heading to East Africa, and families keeping Swahili alive at home.
landing.first: Greetings and respect, family, food and the market, numbers and time, places and getting around, the home, the days of the week and your health, unit by unit.
